daily.title: GST on Free Warranty Replacements: Rules for Manufacturers, Distributors and Importers
daily.summary: Understand GST on free warranty replacements, ITC reversal, distributor transactions, extended warranties and import of replacement parts under CBIC Circular 195/07/2023-GST. An extended warranty bought separately is a separate supply. Bought with the original supply, it may form part of a composite or mixed supply; bought later, it is a distinct taxable supply. Where a foreign OEM sends replacement parts into India free of cost, customs duty and IGST still apply at import on the assessable value, despite the absence of consideration. The Indian subsidiary acting as importer should document the warranty claims to support valuation and any duty-related claims.

daily.title: Importer Need Not Challenge Assessment For Refund After Anti-Dumping Duty Set At Nil: Bombay High Court
daily.summary: The Bombay High Court has held that an importer need not challenge the assessment of bills of entry to claim a refund of provisional anti-dumping duty when the final duty is determined as nil.“The... “The refund becomes automatic after the Second Notification is issued under Section 9A(1) of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975, and the same was required to be processed since the Anti-Dumping Duty was finally determined as 'Nil'.
